10: from sklearn.utils import check_random_state

12: from tslearn.backend import instantiate_backend
13: from tslearn.backend.pytorch_backend import HAS_TORCH
14: from tslearn.utils import  to_time_series, to_time_series_dataset
15: from tslearn.utils.utils import _to_time_series

20: def sigma_gak(dataset, n_samples=100, random_state=None, be=None):
21:     r"""Compute sigma value to be used for GAK.
22: 
23:     This method was originally presented in [1]_.
24: 
25:     Parameters
26:     ----------
27:     dataset : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d) or (n_ts, sz1) or (sz,)
28:         A dataset of time series.
29:         If shape is (n_ts, sz), the dataset is composed of univariate time series.
30:         If shape is (sz,), the dataset is composed of a unique univariate time series.
31:     n_samples : int (default: 100)
32:         Number of samples on which median distance should be estimated.
33:     random_state : integer or numpy.RandomState or None (default: None)
34:         The generator used to draw the samples. If an integer is given, it
35:         fixes the seed. Defaults to the global numpy random number generator.
36:     be : Backend object or string or None
37:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
38:         the NumPy backend is used.
39:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
40:         the PyTorch backend is used.
41:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
42:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
43: 
44:     Returns
45:     -------
46:     float
47:         Suggested bandwidth (:math:`\sigma`) for the Global Alignment kernel.
48: 
49:     Examples
50:     --------
51:     >>> dataset = [[1, 2, 2, 3], [1., 2., 3., 4.]]
52:     >>> float(sigma_gak(dataset=dataset,
53:     ...                 n_samples=200,
54:     ...                 random_state=0))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
55:     2.0...
56: 
57:     See Also
58:     --------
59:     gak : Compute Global Alignment kernel
60:     cdist_gak : Compute cross-similarity matrix using Global Alignment kernel
61: 
62:     References
63:     ----------
64:     .. [1] M. Cuturi, "Fast global alignment kernels,"
65:        ICML 2011.
66:     """
67:     be = instantiate_backend(be, dataset)
68:     dataset = to_time_series_dataset(dataset, be=be)
69: 
70:     return _sigma_gak(dataset, n_samples, random_state, be)
71: 
72: 
73: def _sigma_gak(dataset, n_samples=100, random_state=None, be=None):
74:     if be is None:
75:         be = instantiate_backend(dataset)
76: 
77:     _, sz, d = dataset.shape
78: 
79:     # Remove points with nans from dataset
80:     dataset = dataset.reshape((-1, d))
81:     mask = be.isfinite(be.sum(dataset, axis=-1))
82:     dataset = dataset[mask]
83: 
84:     random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
85:     nb_valid_samples = len(dataset)
86:     replace = nb_valid_samples < n_samples
87:     sample_indices = random_state.choice(
88:         nb_valid_samples,
89:         size=n_samples,
90:         replace=replace
91:     )
92:     dists = be.pdist(
93:         dataset[sample_indices],
94:         metric="euclidean",
95:     )
96:     return be.median(dists) * be.sqrt(sz)
97: 
98: 
99: def gak(s1, s2, sigma=1.0, be=None):
100:     r"""Compute Global Alignment Kernel (GAK) between (possibly
101:     multidimensional) time series and return it.
102: 
103:     .. math::
104: 
105:         \text{gak}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) =
106:             \frac{k(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})}
107:                 {\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x})k(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{y})}}
108: 
109:     where
110: 
111:     .. math::
112: 
113:         k(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) =
114:             \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{A}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})}
115:                 \prod_{i=1}^{ | \pi | }
116:                     \exp \left( - \frac{ \left\| x_{\pi_1(i)} - y_{\pi_2{j}} \right\|^2}{2 \sigma^2} \right)
117: 
118:     It is not required that both time series share the same size, but they must
119:     be the same dimension. GAK was originally presented in [1]_.
120:     This is a normalized version that ensures that :math:`gak(x,x)=1` for all
121:     :math:`x` and :math:`gak(x,y) \in [0, 1]` for all :math:`x, y`.
122: 
123:     Parameters
124:     ----------
125:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
126:         A time series.
127:         If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
128:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
129:         Another time series.
130:         If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
131:     sigma : float (default 1.)
132:         Bandwidth of the internal gaussian kernel used for GAK.
133:     be : Backend object or string or None
134:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
135:         the NumPy backend is used.
136:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
137:         the PyTorch backend is used.
138:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
139:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
140: 
141:     Returns
142:     -------
143:     float
144:         Kernel value
145: 
146:     Examples
147:     --------
148:     >>> float(gak([1, 2, 3], [1., 2., 2., 3.], sigma=2.))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
149:     0.839...
150:     >>> float(gak([1, 2, 3], [1., 2., 2., 3., 4.]))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
151:     0.273...
152: 
153:     See Also
154:     --------
155:     cdist_gak : Compute cross-similarity matrix using Global Alignment kernel
156: 
157:     References
158:     ----------
159:     .. [1] M. Cuturi, "Fast global alignment kernels,"
160:        ICML 2011.
